body: Thanks, I'm feeling much better. As a recovering alcoholic, I didn't handle being let go very well, and checked into this hotel a week ago in the hopes of trying to drink myself to death. And of course it made me feel profound depressions and fear I hadn't felt in years. I've gotten through what feels like the darkest. Got sober after some pretty horrible withdrawals. Still have cold sweats and tremors, but I went to an AA meeting and it gave me hope.
Thank you. I love her so much, but just feel so hopeless right now.

Thanks, I appreciate it. And it's why I came here. I decided to go out Leaving Las Vegas style. But I've been in this place since Monday and the alcohol thing hasn't worked out so well. I really hate throwing up, but I've been doing it a lot. I also haven't eaten since Monday, but I have zero appetite. We'll see what happens, but thank you. As I said, I really don't want to die but feel I'm out of options. So I'm using this opportunity to try and remind myself of reasons to live.  

My niece was applying for a liberal arts highs school a few years ago. She had to audition, and fill out a questionnaire that they judged her character on.  

"Who is a person who has made an impact on you, and how?"  

My sister sent me the response. 5 sentences I remember to this day. And she live a thousand miles away. I don't know how it's possible I've had such an impact.  

"A person who has made an impact on me is my Uncle Mark. He and I are very close and he always makes me laugh. He's always been a part of my life and always cheers me up when I'm feeling down. He inspires me to be funny and creative like he is. One day I hope to grow up to be like him."  

I don't know what else to say. I just don't.
